metadata.title: RenalLogic AI Knowledge Base - Chronic Kidney Disease Risk Assessment
guidelines: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) CKD Evaluation Guidance
metadata.scope_notice: Educational and research rule base. Not an approved clinical decision support tool or diagnostic device.

rules.name: eGFR Stage G1: Normal or High
rules.explanation: eGFR >= 90 mL/min/1.73 m² indicates normal or high glomerular filtration rate according to KDIGO 2024 classification.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 2 (GFR Categories)

rules.name: eGFR Stage G2: Mildly Decreased
rules.explanation: eGFR 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m² indicates mildly decreased filtration. In the absence of markers of kidney damage (such as albuminuria), this may be normal for age.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 2

rules.name: eGFR Stage G3a: Mildly to Moderately Decreased
rules.explanation: eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m² indicates mildly to moderately decreased filtration, representing clinically significant impairment when persistent for >3 months.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 2

rules.name: eGFR Stage G3b: Moderately to Severely Decreased
rules.explanation: eGFR 30-44 mL/min/1.73 m² indicates moderately to severely decreased kidney function with elevated cardiovascular and kidney failure risk.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 2

rules.name: eGFR Stage G4: Severely Decreased
rules.explanation: eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m² indicates severely decreased kidney function requiring proactive complication management and nephrology care.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 2

rules.name: eGFR Stage G5: Kidney Failure
rules.explanation: eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m² represents kidney failure (formerly end-stage renal disease), necessitating kidney replacement therapy planning or conservative care.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 2

rules.name: Albuminuria Stage A1: Normal to Mildly Increased
rules.explanation: UACR < 30 mg/g (< 3 mg/mmol) indicates normal to mildly increased urine albumin excretion.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 3 (Albuminuria Categories)

rules.name: Albuminuria Stage A2: Moderately Increased
rules.explanation: UACR 30-300 mg/g (3-30 mg/mmol) indicates moderately increased albuminuria (microalbuminuria), an early marker of glomerular injury and endothelial dysfunction.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 3

rules.name: Albuminuria Stage A3: Severely Increased
rules.explanation: UACR > 300 mg/g (> 30 mg/mmol) indicates severely increased albuminuria (macroalbuminuria), conferring high progression risk to kidney failure and cardiovascular events.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Chapter 1.2, Table 3

rules.name: Abnormal GFR Marker Detection
rules.explanation: eGFR stages G3a through G5 reflect abnormally reduced filtration (< 60 mL/min/1.73 m²), fulfilling the functional threshold for CKD if sustained for >3 months.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Criteria for CKD Definition

rules.name: Abnormal Albuminuria Marker Detection
rules.explanation: Albuminuria categories A2 and A3 indicate pathological leakage of albumin across the glomerular filtration barrier.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Criteria for CKD Definition

rules.name: Kidney Damage or Functional Marker Detected via eGFR
rules.explanation: An abnormal filtration rate serves as an objective marker of impaired kidney function.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Definition of CKD

rules.name: Kidney Damage Marker Detected via Albuminuria
rules.explanation: Persistent or significant albuminuria serves as an established structural/pathological marker of kidney damage.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Definition of CKD

rules.name: Both eGFR and Albuminuria Within Normal Limits
rules.explanation: Both eGFR and albuminuria are within normal or mildly altered reference ranges without evidence of glomerular damage.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Risk Grid (Green Category)

rules.name: Chronicity Confirmed (>= 3 Months)
rules.explanation: KDIGO strictly defines CKD by the persistence of abnormalities for > 3 months. The documented chronicity satisfies this mandatory diagnostic duration criteria.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Definition of CKD (Requirement of >3 months duration)

rules.name: Abnormal Marker Without 3-Month Chronicity
rules.explanation: Abnormalities are not known to have persisted for 3 months. A single laboratory abnormality must never be diagnosed as CKD; acute kidney injury (AKI) or transient albuminuria must be considered.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Chapter 1: Acute vs. Chronic Distinction

rules.name: Abnormal Marker With Unknown Chronicity
rules.explanation: Chronicity data is missing or unknown. Repeat evaluation in 3 months is necessary to distinguish acute vs chronic renal impairment.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Practice Guideline, Diagnostic Uncertainty Rules

rules.name: Chronicity Not Applicable for Normal Markers
rules.explanation: Because measured filtration and albumin excretion are within normal limits, chronic persistence criteria of kidney damage are not triggered.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Evaluation Flow

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G1 + A1 (Low Risk)
rules.explanation: Normal eGFR with normal albumin excretion corresponds to the green (low risk) category in the KDIGO prognosis heat map.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Green Cell G1-A1)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G2 + A1 (Low Risk)
rules.explanation: Mildly decreased eGFR (60-89 mL/min) with normal albuminuria corresponds to low risk in the absence of other markers of kidney disease.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Green Cell G2-A1)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G1 + A2 (Moderately Increased Risk)
rules.explanation: Normal eGFR with moderately increased albuminuria (30-300 mg/g) confers moderately increased risk (yellow zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Yellow Cell G1-A2)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G2 + A2 (Moderately Increased Risk)
rules.explanation: Mildly decreased eGFR with moderately increased albuminuria confers moderately increased risk (yellow zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Yellow Cell G2-A2)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G3a + A1 (Moderately Increased Risk)
rules.explanation: eGFR 45-59 mL/min with normal albuminuria falls into the moderately increased risk category (yellow zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Yellow Cell G3a-A1)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G3b + A1 (High Risk)
rules.explanation: eGFR 30-44 mL/min confers high risk (orange zone) of CKD progression and cardiovascular mortality even without heavy albuminuria.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Orange Cell G3b-A1)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G3a + A2 (High Risk)
rules.explanation: Mild-to-moderate eGFR decline combined with moderate albuminuria yields high risk (orange zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Orange Cell G3a-A2)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G1 + A3 (High Risk)
rules.explanation: Severe albuminuria (> 300 mg/g) elevates CKD risk to high (orange zone) even when glomerular filtration rate remains preserved.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Orange Cell G1-A3)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G2 + A3 (High Risk)
rules.explanation: Severe albuminuria with mildly reduced eGFR indicates significant glomerular pathology and places the patient in the high risk tier.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Orange Cell G2-A3)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G4 Stage (Very High Risk)
rules.explanation: Severe reduction in eGFR (< 30 mL/min) automatically places the individual in the KDIGO very high risk (red zone) category regardless of albuminuria.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Red Zone Row G4)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G5 Stage (Very High Risk)
rules.explanation: Kidney failure (eGFR < 15 mL/min) confers very high risk of mortality, cardiovascular events, and kidney failure progression (red zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Red Zone Row G5)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G3b + A2 (Very High Risk)
rules.explanation: Moderate-to-severe filtration impairment (30-44 mL/min) combined with moderate albuminuria reaches the very high risk tier (red zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Red Cell G3b-A2)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G3a + A3 (Very High Risk)
rules.explanation: eGFR 45-59 mL/min accompanied by severe albuminuria (> 300 mg/g) represents very high risk (red zone).
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Red Cell G3a-A3)

rules.name: KDIGO Grid: G3b + A3 (Very High Risk)
rules.explanation: eGFR 30-44 mL/min paired with severe albuminuria reflects advanced kidney pathology and very high risk.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Prognosis Heat Map (Red Cell G3b-A3)

rules.name: Clinical Assessment: Confirmed CKD Criteria Met
rules.explanation: Patient meets formal KDIGO 2024 criteria for Chronic Kidney Disease: documented persistent kidney impairment or damage (> 3 months duration) with elevated risk classification.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 CKD Clinical Definition & Classification Guidelines

rules.name: Clinical Assessment: Abnormal Markers with Chronicity Unverified
rules.explanation: Laboratory markers show kidney function impairment or albuminuria, but persistence for >= 3 months is unknown. Confirmation requires repeat evaluation in 3 months before a formal CKD diagnosis can be established.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline Section 1.1: Chronicity Verification Mandate

rules.name: Clinical Assessment: Acute Abnormality Suspected (Non-Persistent)
rules.explanation: Abnormal filtration or albuminuria is reported without 3 months of persistence. This pattern warrants evaluation for Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), acute illness, transient albuminuria, or hemodynamic changes rather than chronic disease.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Guideline: Distinguishing AKI from CKD

rules.name: Clinical Assessment: Normal Baseline Findings
rules.explanation: Current laboratory values (eGFR and UACR) are within normal reference ranges, showing no biochemical evidence of kidney damage or functional decline.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Evaluation Guidelines

rules.name: Etiological Modifier: Diabetes Present
rules.explanation: Diabetes mellitus is the primary etiology of chronic kidney disease worldwide. Co-presence of diabetes accelerates microvascular renal disease.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Chapter on Diabetes and CKD / ADA Standards of Care

rules.name: Etiological Modifier: Hypertension Present
rules.explanation: Systemic hypertension serves as both a primary cause and major driver of CKD progression and cardiorenal events.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Blood Pressure Management in CKD

rules.name: Recommendation: Nephrology Referral Indicated
rules.explanation: KDIGO 2024 guidelines recommend nephrology referral for individuals with eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² (stages G4 and G5) for specialized multi-disciplinary care and renal replacement planning.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Chapter 1.4: Referral Criteria

rules.name: Recommendation: Nephrology Referral for Heavy Albuminuria
rules.explanation: Severe albuminuria (UACR > 300 mg/g) is an independent trigger for nephrologist evaluation due to high risk of rapid progression and glomerulonephritis etiology.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Chapter 1.4: Referral Criteria

rules.name: Surveillance: Annual Monitoring (1x/year)
rules.explanation: Individuals in the KDIGO green or yellow categories should have eGFR and UACR assessed at least annually to screen for or monitor progression.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Monitoring Frequency Guidelines

rules.name: Surveillance: Bi-Annual Monitoring (2x/year)
rules.explanation: High-risk category (orange zone) warrants monitoring eGFR and albuminuria at least twice per year to detect rapid functional decline.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Monitoring Frequency Guidelines

rules.name: Surveillance: Frequent Monitoring (3-4x/year)
rules.explanation: Very high risk category (red zone) requires close laboratory surveillance 3 to 4 times per year to manage electrolyte, mineral, and cardiovascular complications.
rules.source: KDIGO 2024 Monitoring Frequency Guidelines
